newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to decide diplomatic row with Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to decide diplomatic row with Singapore.

text.p: The Malaysian cabinet will decide on Wednesday whether to lay to rest a week-long diplomatic furore with Singapore over disparaging remarks by Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew.

Lee said in a statement on Monday he would ask a local court to delete a remark in an affidavit that the Malaysian state of Johor "was notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings", a blast that infuriated Kuala Lumpur.
Monday's statement followed a rare public apology to Malaysia last week over the remarks, but many Malaysians said a simple apology was inadequate and demanded a retraction.
Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Tuesday declined to comment on Lee's latest statement, telling reporters in the central state of Pahang: "We will tell you after the Cabinet meeting tomorrow."
Mahathir said he was informed of Lee's latest move through a letter sent to him on Monday night.

But the chairman of the youth wing of Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, welcomed Lee's latest move and said the movement did not want the issue to be prolonged.
"We hope what happened will serve as a lesson to everyone and the spirit of good neighbourliness should be upheld," he said.

UMNO youth had earlier threatened to sue the 73-year-old Lee, Singapore's independence leader and first prime minister, after staging protests last week in which they called him "stupid", "senile" and "a bloody idiot".

Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim also welcomed Lee's latest move. "This statement is certainly more positive than his earlier statement," he was quoted as saying by the New Straits Times daily on Tuesday.
Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi called it "a good development".

In his signed statement on Monday, Lee said: "Malaysian government leaders have expressed their wish that statements in my affidavit which have caused offence to the Malaysian people not remain on the record.
"My counsel will apply to court for permission to delete the offending statements so that they will no longer remain on the record," he said.
The controversial remarks were part of an affidavit Lee made in court on January 27 in his libel suit against opposition politician Tang Liang Hong.

Tang fled to Johor Baru, capital of Johor state, immediately after losing a race for parliament in Singapore's general elections on January 2, saying he had received death threats in Singapore. Lee questioned why he would feel safer in Johor.
